  MRSA         → 0.7h (3%)

  Run all 5 campaigns in parallel batched.

Designer: have 8 candidate SMILES. Time budget 2 minutes. Target: VRE. Sequence the in silico panel calls to maximize information per second.

[Designer]: 8 candidates, 2-minute budget = 120s. Tools have widely different latencies; the right strategy is gate-then-confirm: cheap tools knock out failures fast, expensive tools only run on candidates that survived.

PHASE 1 (per-candidate, parallel, ~1s each):
  1. predict_admet (100ms) — instant Lipinski/Veber gate
  2. predict_mic_pathogen (200ms) — primary activity gate
  → Kill any candidate with log10(MIC) > 1.5 or Lipinski viol > 2
  Cost: ~2400ms total
  Expected survivors: ~4/8

PHASE 2 (per-survivor, ~500ms each):
  3. predict_hemolysis (200ms)
  4. score_molecule (350ms) — composite
  → Kill any with composite < 0.5 or hemolysis = high
  Expected survivors: ~2/8

PHASE 3 (per-survivor, ~1.5s each):
  5. predict_resistance_escape (300ms)
  6. predict_synthesis_route (800ms)
  7. find_similar_drugs (400ms) — novelty check
  → Final ranking by composite + escape verdict + cost

PHASE 4 (top-1 only, expensive):
  8. predict_complex_structure (8000ms) — Boltz-2 3D pose
  9. dock_against_target (5000ms) — confirm pose
  → Only the best candidate enters this stage

Total estimated wall-clock: 19 seconds. Well within the 2-minute budget. Buffer for scaffold-hop iteration if any phase produces zero survivors.

DECISION: Begin Phase 1 in parallel across all 8 candidates.

  9. dock_against_target (5000ms) — confirm pose
  → Only the best candidate enters this stage

Design a broad-spectrum candidate active against: VRE, MRSA (gram+ pair). Constraint: PBP / ribosomal targets.

[Designer]: Broad-spectrum design against 2 pathogens (VRE, MRSA). The challenge: each pathogen has a distinct resistome.

<tool_call>name: get_pathogen_resistome

[Tool]: returns resistome briefing per pathogen

[Designer]: Cross-pathogen analysis:
  VRE          → vanA D-Ala:D-Lac
  MRSA         → mecA → PBP2a allosteric site

[Designer]: SHARED VULNERABILITY: β-lactam transpeptidase. Anchor scaffold on this class, then optimize entry strategy per pathogen.

Design strategy:
  1. Core pharmacophore: β-lactam transpeptidase engagement
  2. Entry strategy:
     - For gram+ (VRE, MRSA): thick peptidoglycan permeable scaffold; charge < 2+
     - For gram- (): siderophore-conjugate or low-MW (< 350 Da) for porin entry
     - For Mtb: lipophilic core for mycolic-acid wall passage
  3. Resistance avoidance:
     - Avoid β-lactam classes that bind canonical PBPs
     - Use covalent tail or allosteric handle to escape single-mutation
